newsitem.title: CROATIA: EBRD signs its first private sector deal in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: EBRD signs its first private sector deal in Bosnia.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) said it signed on Friday its first private sector investment in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

The EBRD invested two million German marks (ECU 1.1 million) in the share capital of Hrvatska Banka, Mostar, acquiring a 17-percent stake in the bank, the EBRD said in a statement obtained by Reuters.
"(The investment) is designed to support a well-managed and dynamic young private bank and help restore confidence in the country's financial sector after years of war," the EBRD said.
The investment will be conditional upon an extensive training programme in the form of a two-year twinning arrangement with a foreign bank.

It will allow Hrvatska Banka to increase its funding base in support of an anticipated growth in lending and investment operations, to implement a viable business plan and to attract other shareholders and additional funding resources, the EBRD said.
Hrvatska Banka was founded in 1992 in the Croat section of the southern Bosnian town of Mostar, divided by Moslems and Croats during a vicious 4-1/2-year war.
It has two branches and 18 units, and plans to open a branch in Sarajevo in 1997 and another branch in Tuzla thereafter.

"The EBRD's equity investment in Hrvatska Banka is in line with its strategy in the financial sector of Bosnia-Herzegovina which aims to strenthen private financial intermediaries, to increase the ability of the economy to absorb foreign funding and to ensure efficient allocation of resources to small and medium-sized enterprise sector," David Hexter, the deputy vice- president of the EBRD, said upon signing.
He said the EBRD was working on additional equity investment opportunities in other parts of the country. -- Davor Huic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
